text:
taylor: FYI planning a short maintenance tonight 23:00 UTC (45m window) to roll a runtime kernel update and a small batching config tweak. Expected user-visible impact: brief token latency spike (~100ms) while nodes drain, and a 5–10m period of increased error rate risk on a small subset during pod restarts. Preparing customer comms + statuspage snippet below, please review and flag any blockers. :gear:

deploy-bot: job scheduled: id=rb-2026-1769456123, run_at=2026-03-21T23:00:00Z, affected=hosted-runtime-pool-2 :robot_face:

kevin: Can we do a region-stagger? EU first (23:00 UTC), then APAC at 00:00 UTC +30m buffer. Also, if we see >1% 5xx for 3 consecutive minutes we should abort and hold on the rollout — want to capture rollback criteria in this thread.

priya: +1 to stagger. Draft statuspage snippet below for EU-first roll (copy/paste friendly):

```
Component: Hosted Inference Runtime (EU)
Status: Maintenance in progress
Impact: Short-lived increased latency and potential 5xx for a small fraction of requests while we roll runtime kernels.
ETA: ~15–30 minutes
Update: We are rolling servers in small batches and monitoring errors; will post another update when complete.
```

priya: Draft customer email (short):

```
Subject: Planned maintenance tonight — short impact expected

Hi —
We will perform a short maintenance on our EU inference hosts tonight at 23:00 UTC to deploy performance and reliability fixes. Most requests will be unaffected; a small number may see slightly higher latency or transient errors for a few minutes. If you rely on strict latency SLAs or have peak traffic at that time, reply and we can coordinate a deferral or use a dedicated lane.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations
```

support-bot: Recommend targeted broadcast only to customers with heavy EU usage and any active Dedicated seats. Suggested support canned reply to triage incoming tickets: 

```
Thanks for reporting — we are currently performing a planned maintenance on EU inference hosts. Can you share the request ID and approximate timestamp? We will prioritize any customer-facing errors and escalate to the rollout team if your traffic is impacted beyond the expected window.
```

kevin: For rollback criteria: abort if sustained 5xx >1% for 3m OR p95 latency >500ms for 5m on the affected pool. Rollback action = immediate traffic hold + route to warm fallback pool (cpu-fallback-1) and open emergency incident channel. Also include a quick smoke checklist post-roll:
- Check 200s on /v1/generate for 10 warm requests across 3 zones
- Verify KV cache warmup < 2s on first-key loads
- Confirm no increase in model hallucination regressions on eval set (smoke-eval-quick)

kevin: Example rollback command (ops-only):

```
# hold rollout and reroute traffic
redwoodctl rollout hold --job rb-2026-1769456123
redwoodctl route set --pool hosted-runtime-pool-2 --fallback cpu-fallback-1
```

taylor: Approve staggered plan and rollback thresholds. Priya — can you publish the statuspage snippet and queue the customer email for selective send? Kevin — you'll run the smoke checklist and monitor metrics during the window? :thumbsup:

priya: I'll patch the statuspage now and queue the targeted email (EU high-usage + Dedicated). I'll also create a 10min canary job to monitor 5xx/p95 and tag alerts to the mobilized incident channel. Planning to post the first status update at rollout start, then a completion update. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: maintenance start scheduled for 2026-03-21T23:00:00Z. Notifications queued to: EU heavy-usage list, Dedicated seats. Will post 'started' event to #incidents when run.

support-bot: Saved canned replies in Zendesk macro "EU runtime maintenance Mar21" and attached monitoring runbook.

kevin: leaving a quick note: if we hit rollback, owners = @kevin (rollout ops), @taylor (eng-platform), @priya (statuspage/support).

taylor: perfect. thanks all — will stand by in the channel at start time. :eyes:
